metadata.title: Odin OS: Hardware-Enforced Physical Memory Protection and Wordline Gating for Sovereign AI Agents
metadata.description:
Odin OS is a bare-metal, zero-allocation (#![no_std]) 64-bit RISC-V microkernel that anchors autonomous AI agent capability boundaries directly into physical silicon memory comparators. Operating on the central axiom that state that cannot prove its right to exist cannot be committed, Odin OS enforces capability containment via cache-line aligned 256-byte binary tokens termed TransitionDeeds.

By leveraging RISC-V Physical Memory Protection (PMP) registers in Top-of-Range (TOR) mode during privileged Machine Mode (M-Mode) execution, the CPU hardware comparators dynamically lock down all out-of-bounds physical addresses by forcing Write Enable to zero (WE = 0). This publication includes empirical proof executing against local neural inference on google/gemma-4-e4b: authorized mutations commit in a single clock cycle, while adversarial prompt injection jailbreaks trigger hardware Store Access Faults (mcause = 0x07), leaving zero bits flipped in physical memory.
